clue.text: Military jumpers for destocking, original shade

parts.note: paras = paratroopers, soldiers who jump from aircraft

indicators.note: to destock is to empty a shop of its stock, so the word loses its contents and keeps only its shell

parts.note: ORIGINAL emptied of its inside letters leaves O…L

explanation.surface: A military surplus shop clears out its stock of paratroopers' sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' wants to be sweaters, which fits the shop picture of destocking; here they are soldiers who jump from planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: this is a sunshade, and shade is what it gives.

clue.text: Rodents beneath edges of plateau rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece written beneath comes second
the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of PLATEAU

explanation.surface: Small animals living under the rim of a high plateau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beneath' is a down-clue instruction: the rodents go below the plateau's edges in the grid, just as the surface places them.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this light, porous volcanic stone is one kind of rock.

clue.text: Note Russian jet circling on eastern course

parts.note: re, the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: to circle round is to turn back on itself, so the jet's name runs backwards

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: A pilot records a Russian fighter circling on an easterly heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like the flight path of the circling jet; it is a course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prescribed course of diet or exercise is also called by this word.

clue.text: Delightful guest ignoring tech boss

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so IT is removed

explanation.surface: A charming visitor pays no attention to the head of the tech firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tech boss' reads as one phrase, a tech company chief; split it, and 'tech' is IT while 'boss' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the person who oversees your work is your boss.

clue.text: Temporary vicar Old Jock Hume entirely stripped off

indicators.note: every word has its outer letters peeled away, like clothes stripped off

parts.note: OLD without its outer O and D

explanation.surface: An elderly Scot called Hume took all his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jock is a Scotsman in British slang, so the surface pictures a naked old Scot; the names are only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a stand-in clergyman or doctor covering for an absent one is called this.

clue.text: Dull periods periodically rotating US spies

indicators.note: at regular periods, so every other letter is taken
turning round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of PERIODS
the CIA, the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: American agents are moved round in dreary stints of duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periods periodically' uses the same word twice: the first is the fodder, the second tells you to take every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: writing that is like prose rather than poetry is flat and unimaginative.

clue.text: Maritime campaigner Samuel, originator of sea pumps

parts.note: Samuel Plimsoll campaigned for the load line on ships

indicators.note: the letter that starts a word originates it

explanation.surface: A tribute to Samuel Plimsoll as the inventor of pumps that drain water from ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea pumps' suggests bilge pumps; pumps are also light canvas shoes, named in Britain after the Plimsoll line their rubber rim resembled.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Britain light canvas gym shoes are called pumps as well as by this name.

clue.text: Work over — drink up!

parts.note: O = over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: The job's done, so drink up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work over' and 'drink up' read as end-of-shift phrases; 'Work' is the definition and 'over' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Latin word for a work, used especially of a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Lad who went for a dip feeling sick, beset by pains

definitions.text: Lad who went for a dip

explanation.surface: A boy who went swimming came out sick and aching all over.
explanation.walkthrough: The lad's dip was in the River Styx: his mother dipped the infant in it to make him invulnerable, holding him by the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: the Greek hero's famous dip in the Styx is the story behind his one weak heel.

clue.text: Tory eating meat pie without base — excellent!

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, the last letter
the outer word takes the others inside it

explanation.surface: A Conservative tucks into a pie with no pastry bottom and pronounces it splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative party, abbreviated Con.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: in dated northern English slang the word is an exclamation meaning splendid.

clue.text: Study gazing at the stars?

definitions.meaning: British slang for cramming hard before an exam
mug is slang for face, and a star-gazer's face points skyward

explanation.surface: Is studying just staring at the sky?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, where the phrase is taken literally as a face turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: British slang for swotting, and a literal face-raised reading for someone watching the sky.

clue.text: One having a small bite here in Mexico?

definitions.meaning: the tiniest dog breed, whose nip is correspondingly small
a large state in northern Mexico

explanation.surface: Someone grabbing a snack while visiting Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A small bite' looks like a snack; it is a little dog's nip. The breed is named after the Mexican state.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the smallest dog breed, and the northern Mexican state it was named after.

clue.text: Firm undertaking involving mass trade-off

parts.note: Co. = company, a firm; front of the outside
a promise is an undertaking; back of the outside

explanation.surface: A company's pledge includes a large-scale concession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' wants to be an adjective describing the undertaking; it is a noun, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a settlement where each side gives something up to get something.

clue.text: Temporary setback as Mike bales out of small airship

indicators.note: to bail out is to jump from an aircraft

parts.note: a blimp is a small non-rigid airship
Mike = M in the NATO alphabet; removed

explanation.surface: A short-lived hitch when a crewman parachutes from a blimp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bales out' is the jump from the aircraft, so the airship picture tells you to remove a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brief dip on a graph, hence a short-lived hitch.

clue.text: Angry Lebanon regularly denying former queen

indicators.note: angry letters are stirred up, rearranged
at regular intervals, so every other letter

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of DENYING

explanation.surface: A furious Lebanon refuses, time after time, to recognise a one-time queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Both LEBANON and the alternate letters of 'denying' go into the mix together.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Henry VIII's second wife was queen of England until her execution in 1536.

clue.text: Painter & decorator getting nice Hello! mag spread

indicators.note: the letters are spread about, scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A tradesman lands a flattering spread in Hello! magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine famous for glossy photo spreads. 'Painter & decorator' is a humble trade, but here it is the artist who painted the Sistine Chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: the Renaissance artist both painted and decorated the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

clue.text: Clumsy, poor actor is deft when tipsy

indicators.note: tipsy letters stagger about, so IS DEFT is rearranged

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor

explanation.surface: A bad actor is only nimble once he has had a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deft' sits right beside 'Clumsy' as its opposite, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: having hands like hams, too big to handle things delicately.

clue.text: City in Turkmenistan bulldozed

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A town in Turkmenistan has been flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulldozed' looks like an anagram indicator for Turkmenistan; the city simply runs across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Turkey's largest city.

clue.text: Little Tom's out of bed, which is an encouraging sign

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so his is Thumb's

explanation.surface: The little boy is up and about, a good sign he is feeling better.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is' in the surface but as a possessive in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the raised-thumb gesture signals approval or encouragement.

clue.text: His job is to sort out the classroom

definitions.text: His job is to sort out the classroom

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange into order

explanation.surface: A description of a teacher keeping order in class.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: read plainly it defines a teacher, and 'sort out' tells you to rearrange THE CLASSROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: keeping a class in order is exactly a male teacher's job.

clue.text: Game served up in Moonrakers Inn, Eton

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom
the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: moonrakerS INN ETon, to be read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A game is on the menu at a pub called the Moonrakers near Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' also points at the answer's game, where you serve. Eton is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a racket sport is one kind of game.

clue.text: National Insurance collected in tax year is an extravagance

parts.note: VAT = value added tax; the outside
the first letters of National Insurance, the UK payroll contribution

explanation.surface: Paying National Insurance within the tax year feels like a luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's sales tax and National Insurance its payroll contribution, so the surface reads like a tax return; 'tax year' is split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a self-indulgent luxury, as in a vanity project.

clue.text: Crazy to write off British force

indicators.note: to write something off is to cancel it

explanation.surface: It would be mad to dismiss the British armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is everyday British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a land-based military force.

clue.text: Something from the Savoy Hotel, a grip perhaps

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A souvenir from London's Savoy Hotel, maybe a holdall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savoy Hotel' reads as one place; split it. The Savoy is also a London theatre where Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas, the Savoy operas, were first staged.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Gilbert and Sullivan's Savoy operas are the classic works of this comic genre.

clue.text: Turkish sweet hearts left entertained by Ms Gardner

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is inside her home

parts.note: Ava Gardner, the Hollywood actress; the outside

explanation.surface: Ava Gardner charms a sweetheart who is being left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet hearts' reads as sweethearts; split it, and 'Turkish sweet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a sesame-paste confection eaten across Turkey and the Middle East.

clue.text: Daughter in law initially goes off puzzle book

indicators.note: the initial letters of the words before it
something that goes off departs, so those initials leave the puzzle word

parts.note: first letters of DAUGHTER IN LAW; removed

explanation.surface: A daughter-in-law walks out in a huff over a puzzle book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle book' is two jobs: 'puzzle' is the word to cut and 'book' the definition, a Jane Austen novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Jane Austen's 1815 novel.

clue.text: Swiss city hosting today's Facebook lead?

indicators.note: a host holds its guest inside

parts.note: Facebook's parent company is now called Meta; goes inside

explanation.surface: A Swiss city is home to Facebook's current top story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a news lead, the top story; it is the metal, and the question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the heavy grey element is a common, non-precious metal.

clue.text: Boredom leads to extremely nasty nationalists urging insurrection

indicators.note: the leading letters of each word

explanation.surface: Being bored drives very unpleasant nationalists to call for an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads to' reads as 'causes'; split it, and 'leads' asks for the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the French word for listless weariness, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Where toy manufacturer is dependent on elf 'n' safety at work?

definitions.text: Where toy manufacturer is dependent on elf 'n' safety at work?

parts.note: reads as a factory's location; the toy maker is Father Christmas

parts.words: dependent on elf 'n' safety at work?
parts.note: mimics 'health and safety at work'; really his workshop relies on elves

explanation.surface: A toy factory whose output depends on following workplace safety rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elf 'n' safety' is a play on 'health and safety', the British shorthand for workplace regulations; Father Christmas's home is traditionally in Lapland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: the region of northern Finland is Santa's traditional home, where elves make the toys.

clue.text: Pardon means roughly twenty to be discharged

indicators.note: the letters are roughed up, rearranged
discharged of its contents, emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A pardon means about twenty prisoners will be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' fits the prison picture of release; here it means emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a general pardon granted to a whole group of offenders.
